## The Packages

To use PsyR to calculate confidence intervals over contrast effects, we will utilise a workflow with functions from [afex](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/afex/versions/1.4-1) to implement ANOVA models, and [emmeans](https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/) to obtain estimated marginal means and the required contrast estimates. So let's load those packages, and any others that are helpful for our workflow.

```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(afex)
library(emmeans)
library(PsyR)
library(tidyverse)
```

## The Data

The `distraction` dataframe contains the results of a (3 x 3) within-subjects factorial design. Here,  *N* = 10 participants were asked to respond within a period of time to the presentation of a target stimulus viewed under three levels of auditory distraction and three levels of visual distraction (*p* = 9). The dependent variable was the number of trials out of 20 for which Ps responded within the required time period to the target stimulus, with a higher score indicating better performance.

Let's load the data, then call the `head()` function to print the first 5 rows.

```{r loaddata}
data(distraction)
head(distraction, 5)
```

Also, let's tidy up the data, labelling the levels of our independent variables for greater clarity.

```{r, sortfactors}
distraction <- distraction %>%
  mutate(
    Auditory = fct_relevel(Auditory, 'Low', 'Medium', 'High'),
    Visual = fct_relevel(Visual, 'None', 'Dissimilar', 'Similar'),
    Subject = factor(Subject)
  )
```

Next, let's visualise our data. Doing so allows us to more intuitively understand its layout.

```{r plotdata}
distraction %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Auditory, y = Performance, colour = Visual, fill = Visual, shape = Visual)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3, aes(group = Visual)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", aes(group = Visual)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21:24)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)
```

Let's prepare to run some statistical tests!

Here we will create the building blocks for first an ANOVA output, and later our SCIs. To start, let's create the object `mod` by calling the `aov_ez()` function. Of note, defining `mod` in this way will enable emmeans to compute estimated marginal means from which to apply contrasts of interest. Place the `Subject` column in the ID argument, `Performance` as our dependent variable, `distraction` as our dataframe, and `Auditory` and `Visual` as our within-subjects factors.

```{r, aov}

# perform the statistical model
mod <- aov_ez(
  id = "Subject",
  dv = "Performance",
  data = distraction,
  within = c("Auditory", "Visual")
)
knitr::kable(mod, digits = 3)
```

## Define contrasts

First for the auditory factor (A)

```{r, audcontrasts}
emms_aud <- emmeans(mod, c("Auditory"))

aud_contrasts <- list(
  "hvlm" = c(0.5, 0.5, -1),
  "hvl" = c(1, -1, 0)
)

aud_fx <- contrast(emms_aud, aud_contrasts)
knitr::kable(aud_fx, digits = 3)
```

Now for visual (factor B)

```{r, viscontrasts}
emms_vis <- emmeans(mod, c("Visual"))
emms_vis

vis_contrasts <- list(
  "none_vs_some" = c(1, -0.5, -0.5),
  "sim_vs_dissim" = c(0, 1, -1)
)

vis_fx <- contrast(emms_vis, vis_contrasts)
vis_fx
```

And now the interaction contrasts -

```{r, intcontrasts}
emms_int <- emmeans(mod, c("Auditory","Visual"))
emms_int

int_fx <- contrast(emms_int, interaction = list(aud_contrasts, vis_contrasts))
int_fx

```

## Simultaneous Confidence Intervals

Now we're ready to compute SCIs

```{r scis}
output <- psyci(
  model = mod, 
  contrast_tables = c(aud_fx, vis_fx, int_fx), 
  method = "bf"
) 

display <- output %>%
  unclass() %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(
    Auditory = coalesce(Auditory_custom, contrast),
    Visual = coalesce(Visual_custom, contrast)
  ) %>%
  select(estimate:psyr_p_value, Auditory, Visual) %>%
  relocate(Auditory, Visual)

display[1, 2] <- NA
display[2, 2] <- NA
display[3, 1] <- NA
display[4, 1] <- NA

knitr::kable(display, digits = 3)
```
Now run the same thing, but with individual 95% confidence intervals


```{r individual_cis}
output_ind <- psyci(
  model = mod, 
  contrast_tables = c(aud_fx, vis_fx, int_fx),
  method = "ind"
)

display_ind <- output_ind %>%
  unclass() %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(
    Auditory = coalesce(Auditory_custom, contrast),
    Visual = coalesce(Visual_custom, contrast)
  ) %>%
  select(estimate:psyr_p_value, Auditory, Visual) %>%
  relocate(Auditory, Visual)

display_ind[1, 2] <- NA
display_ind[2, 2] <- NA
display_ind[3, 1] <- NA
display_ind[4, 1] <- NA

knitr::kable(display_ind, digits = 3)
```
